analysis.title: Global Weekly Kickstart: Earnings Season Arrives with a High Bar
key_insights: Consensus expects Q3 S&P 500 EPS growth of 27% y/y, versus 33% in Q2 excluding accounting distortions. AI infrastructure beneficiaries generate more than half of this quarter's growth.
GS's US team expects companies to beat consensus again, supported by strong economic data and positive earnings-revision breadth. Median-stock EPS growth slows from 14% to 9%, so growth is narrow.
Most hyperscalers report in the final week of October. By then roughly 70% of S&P 500 market cap will have reported.
Europe consensus is for 23% EPS growth, or 16% excluding Commodities. Positive revision momentum, improving PMIs and euro weakness support results in line with expectations or a modest beat.
Global equities rose 0.6% last week alongside Copper (+2.5%) and Brent (+2.1%). Energy and Defensives led, Cyclicals lagged, and Industrials was the weakest sector.
The S&P 500 hit another all-time high and is up 14% YTD. STOXX Europe is up 7%, driven by earnings and resilient despite the Energy and Rates shock.

Calendar this week: US CPI and retail sales, several Fed speaking engagements including Chairman Warsh, UK August monthly GDP, Euro Area September inflation, China money, credit, inflation and trade data, and India CPI.

GS macro forecasts: S&P 500 from 7812 to 8000 (3m), 8300 (6m) and 8700 (12m), 11.4% upside. STOXX 600 from 632 to 695 at 12m. US 10Y yield from 5.2% to 4.4% at 12m. Brent from $104.7 to $75 at 12m. Gold from $4185 to $5235 at 12m.
GS top-down 2026 EPS growth for the S&P 500 is 36% versus 32% consensus bottom-up. For 2027, GS is at 11% versus 15% consensus.
Consensus 2026E S&P 500 sales growth is 12.0% and EPS growth is 31.9%, with 2027E EPS growth of 15.4%. IT sector 2026E EPS growth is 86.7% on 40.7% sales growth, and Energy 2026E EPS growth is 84.9%.
GS Bull/Bear Market Indicator reads 68%. Shiller PE is 41.3 (98th percentile), unemployment 4.2%, ISM 54.5 and core inflation 2.4%.
Valuation: 12m forward P/E is 19.4 for the US, 18.5 for the US ex Big Tech and 16.5 for the AC World index. The Japan, Europe and UK readings run lower.

GS sector weights: US overweight Materials and Health Care. Europe overweight Financials, IT and Communication Services, underweight Consumer Discretionary and Health Care. Japan and APxJ overweight Financials and IT.

earnings_insights: Q3 2026 S&P 500 EPS growth: consensus estimate +27% y/y, versus 33% in Q2 excluding accounting distortions. Not yet reported, season is starting.
GS US team expects companies to beat consensus again. Median-stock EPS growth is expected to slow from 14% to 9%.
Q3 2026 Europe EPS growth: consensus estimate +23% y/y, or +16% excluding Commodities. GS expects results broadly in line or a modest beat.
Full-year consensus bottom-up EPS growth: S&P 500 +31.9% in 2026E and +15.4% in 2027E, STOXX 600 +20.4% and +8.6%, MSCI AC World +35.0% and +16.2%.

risk_factors: The bar is high: consensus S&P 500 EPS growth of 27% leaves less room for a beat.
Earnings growth is concentrated in AI infrastructure beneficiaries, with more than half of the quarter's growth, while median-stock EPS growth slows from 14% to 9%.
Energy and Rates shock weighing on European equities.
Shiller PE at 41.3 sits in the 98th percentile.
